prompt: Write the body (about 150 words) of an insurer's answer to a personal injury petition in Texas: a general denial and three affirmative defenses that fit a hit while turning left. Plain text. Call the parties only 'Plaintiff' and 'Defendant'. No names, placeholders, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1066; do not mention it.)
text:
Defendant generally denies each and every allegation contained in Plaintiff's Original Petition and demands strict proof thereof by a preponderance of the evidence, as required by the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure.

For its first affirmative defense, Defendant asserts that the collision was caused, in whole or in part, by Plaintiff's own negligence, including failure to keep a proper lookout, failure to yield the right-of-way, and driving at a speed greater than was reasonable and prudent under the conditions then existing. Under Chapter 33 of the Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code, any recovery must be reduced by the percentage of responsibility attributed to Plaintiff.

For its second affirmative defense, Defendant asserts proportionate responsibility under Chapter 33, and requests that the trier of fact determine the percentage of responsibility of each claimant, defendant, settling person, and responsible third party, and that any judgment be limited accordingly.

For its third affirmative defense, Defendant asserts that Plaintiff failed to mitigate damages by failing to follow reasonable medical advice and by incurring medical expenses that were not reasonable or necessary. Defendant reserves the right to amend this answer as discovery proceeds.
